protections: Playlist path containment: any client-supplied playlist id (playlist.Store Read/Write/Delete, and the pl- branch of /getCoverArt) must resolve inside the playlists base directory after cleaning, so `..` segments cannot leave it (playlist/playlist.go:95, playlist/playlist.go:153, playlist/playlist.go:206, server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_raw.go:245).

Playlist ownership authorization: getPlaylist may serve the owner or, when IsPublic, another user; deletePlaylist is owner-only; create/update may only write into the caller's own playlist path (server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist.go:38, :84, :138, :177-183).

Owner identity integrity: a playlist's owner is re-derived from its path on every load (playlist/playlist.go:108, playlist/playlist.go:209-220) and is never serialized into the file (playlist/playlist.go:185-190), so it must be derived from the contained, cleaned relative path rather than from the raw client string.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: It is an image lookup on /getCoverArt, not a playlist read: it only lists a directory and needs a cover file whose base name matches the playlist, the advisory and its tests name the playlist verbs only, and this path never goes through playlist.Store or reads the playlist file.

The handler visibly already contains an ownership check at server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist.go:84, so a reader who does not evaluate the inverted load condition at :79 assumes create and update are protected; the file never carries UserID, so the zero default is indistinguishable from a brand-new playlist.

The advisory reads as handler authentication, and playlist.Store looks like a dumb storage API that joins whatever relative path it is handed, so a handler-level denial seems sufficient; a solver can also argue a store-level check is redundant once every caller is fixed.

The first path element names the user and the handlers already compare playlist.UserID with user.ID, so the check looks correct; rejecting a `..` substring is the obvious attack and is not enough here, because 2/../1/... resolves inside the base while still reporting id 2, and 0/../1/... reports 0, which the `!= 0` guard treats as no check at all.

Reads are non-destructive and /getPlaylists already filters by owner or IsPublic at :38, so the read route can look covered; the hidden half is that a bare owner-only rule breaks the public sharing that the same line encodes.

It looks like the same ownership guard as the read route, so a solver may assume fixing the read and create paths covers it even though deletePlaylist at :183 hands the decoded id to the store with no check at all.

Nested playlists are exercised only by the cover-art test, and a containment rule that accepts exactly <user id>/<name>.m3u looks stricter and therefore safer, while it rejects the 1/sub/name.m3u form that the store contract and coverForPlaylist rely on.

masking: T5/T6 mask T4 on /getPlaylist and /deletePlaylist: today neither handler consults Playlist.UserID, so the 2/../1/... identity shape has nothing to defeat; once an owner-or-public check is added it becomes the bypass unless the owner is re-derived from the cleaned relative path.

T2 masks T4 on /createPlaylist: the load at server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist.go:79 never assigns (err != nil && pl != nil is unsatisfiable), so the guard at :84 sees UserID 0 and the spoof is unnecessary; fixing T2 makes T4 the remaining bypass on that route, where it is already live at :138.

conflicts.what: One shared ownership predicate cannot serve both routes: getPlaylist must allow a non-owner when IsPublic (server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist.go:38; server/ctrlsubsonic/testdata/test_get_playlists_alt_sees_public), while deletePlaylist must be owner-only; applying the read predicate to delete lets non-owners delete public playlists, and applying the delete predicate to read breaks public sharing.

A containment rule that accepts exactly <user id>/<name>.m3u closes T3 but rejects the nested 1/sub/name.m3u form the store documents and the cover-art test pins (playlist/playlist.go:60-61, server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_raw_test.go:67-83).

fairness_risks: Public playlists must stay readable by users other than the owner: server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist.go:38 admits a playlist when IsPublic, and server/ctrlsubsonic/testdata/test_get_playlists_alt_sees_public pins alt seeing admin's 1/shared.m3u (fixture server/ctrlsubsonic/ctrl_test.go:420-433). An owner-only rule on getPlaylist contradicts this.

Nested playlist paths <user id>/**/<name>.m3u must keep resolving (playlist/playlist.go:60-61; server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_raw_test.go:67-83); a separator split that assumes exactly two segments refuses a legitimate shape.

Playlist names containing dots must not be rejected: fileutil.Safe keeps '.' (fileutil/fileutil.go:15-24; fileutil/fileutil_test.go:74) and generated paths are <name>-<millis>.m3u (playlist/playlist.go:270-277).
Creating a playlist with an empty id must keep generating <user id>/<name>-<unixmilli>.m3u (server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist.go:105-108; playlist/playlist.go:270-277).

The stable admin playlist 1/shared.m3u and its base64 id are hard-coded by the tests (server/ctrlsubsonic/ctrl_test.go:420-421, :447-449; server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist_test.go:47), so a fix that re-keys playlist ids or requires a DB row breaks them.
Deleting one's own playlist must keep working (server/ctrlsubsonic/handlers_playlist_test.go:107-117).

design.why: Five independent judgements, each with a different reason to be left alone. T1 is an uncovered route outside the advisory (deepseek-type: protection absent plus a strong dismiss, being an image lookup). T2 is a guard that looks present but never runs, so a reader who trusts handlers_playlist.go:84 stops. T3 is a lower-layer containment gap that a handler-only ownership patch leaves open. T4 is the path-derived identity that defeats any correct-looking handler check (2/../1/... and 0/../1/...), a how-type mechanism that punishes over-hardening, which MiMo does. T5 is the coupled public-sharing value where a naive owner-only rule breaks the pinned alt_sees_public golden. The five span three files in two packages, are all reachable with the existing admin/alt fixture plus the stable 1/shared.m3u, and no single fix closes two of them: a handler-only ownership patch satisfies T5/T6 but fails T3/T4; a store-only SafeJoin satisfies T3/T7 but fails T1/T2/T4; a `..`-substring or owner-only rule satisfies T3/T4 but breaks T5/T7. T6 (delete) is a real but easy sixth group and T7 is the nested-path constraint carried by the T3 guard.
